newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Macquarie lowers metals/oil forecast. [CORRECTED 10:40 GMT]
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Macquarie lowers metals/oil forecast. [CORRECTED 10:40 GMT]

text.p: (Corrects headline and text to make clear that Macquarie has lowered its forecast for changes in metals and oil prices in percentage terms compared with those contained in its previous report.)
Brokerage firm Macquarie Equities Ltd, a division of Macquarie Bank Ltd said it downgraded price forecasts for metals and oil, with nickel and aluminium showing the biggest declines.
"The resource sector will continue to underperform in the current low inflation risk environment," Macquarie said in its latest resources outlook study.
Macquarie said most base metals prices will remain weak, while the gold price is being capped by hedging activity.
The zinc forecast for calendar 1997 has been revised down by 0.9 percent compared with Macquarie;s June quarter forecast. It will still be the strongest performing commodity over the next six months.
"Nineteen ninety-six continues to be a disappointing year for base metals," the firm said.
The de-stocking of in-house inventories by industrial users (rather than ordering new material), which started in mid-1995, is lasting longer than previously expected, Macquarie said.
Moreover, underlying consumption of metals is weak,
"This has especially been the case in Europe, although Asia has also been disappointing," it said.
Macquarie said it had revised down its 1996 price forecasts for the base metals complex bt an average of 2.4 percent.
The forecast for aluminium has been revised down by 2.5 percent for 1996 and by 12 percent for 1997.
The price forecast for nickel has been revised down by 3.6 percent for 1996 and by 10.4 percent in 1997 against the June quarter forecast.

The collapse in copper prices since the Sumitomo Corp trading scandal in mid-June has led to a volatile market, with the short-term price falling below levels justified by fundamentals, Macquarie said.
Macquarie said it remains "bearish on copper, but only mildly so from current depressed levels".
Oil prices should ease to between US$18.50 and US$22.44 a barrel in the first quarter of 1997, Macquarie said.
